title: The Best Score Among the First Players When Scores Only Rise

concept.title: A Fenwick tree can store a maximum instead of a sum, because the values only grow
body: The scores of `n` players are given. An operation **raises** the score of one player; another asks for the **highest score among the first `x` players**. For the scores `3 9 4 1` the highest among the first three is 9; after raising the fourth player to 12 the highest among all four is 12. Scanning the first `x` scores for every question takes O(n).

The Fenwick tree does not have to store sums. Replace "add" by "maximum": the cell `t[i]` holds the **maximum** of the scores that the cell covers (the last `i & -i` players ending at `i`). To read the maximum of a prefix, jump down as before and take the largest value met on the way. To raise a score, go up as before and set `t[j] = max(t[j], y)` for every cell that covers the player.

This works **only because the scores never decrease**: after a raise the old maximum of a cell is either still correct or replaced by the new score, so `max` is enough. If a score could fall, a covered cell would have to be recomputed from its children, which is what a segment tree does. Each operation costs O(log n).

statement: The scores of `n` players are given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` raises the score of the player `x` to `y` (never lowers it); type 2 `x 0` asks for the highest score among the players `1` to `x`. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of players and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the scores of the players.

Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, the score of the player `x` is raised to `y` (`y` is not smaller than the current score). If `t = 2`, print the highest score among the players `1` to `x` (`y` is 0).
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: A raise never lowers a score.

examples.note: The highest among the first three is 9; after the raise the highest among four is 12: 9 12.

hints: Store maxima in the cells of the tree instead of sums.
A raise sets t[j] = max(t[j], y) along the update path.
A prefix maximum is the largest cell value met on the query path.

solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).
